plan.name: Run each Python check with its own driver
plan.summary: Explicit Python application conformance invocations use the regular staged file identified jointly by their selected check source and script argument resolved from working_dir, preserving application-root containment, traversal and symlink refusals; ordinary execution and startup imports use that driver, while legacy applications and non-conformance startup retain the manifest driver, with no manifest schema change. This intentionally replaces the different-manifest-driver refusal in python_application_gate_accept_test.go and the corresponding contract comment in python_application_execution_accept_test.go, while retaining shared-driver configurations, literal arguments and environment, one immutable application snapshot and dependency image, authenticated collection and exact selected-declaration binding. Larger checking determines bound declarations and the preceding step's successful base execution, transition, exhaustive-state and attempted-step prerequisites separately for each invocation: a driver missing any required bound constant has no larger run or larger record, a bound-declaring invocation with failed prerequisites retains its own original driver and explicit skipped reasons without execution, and the shared larger TLC result is obtained once only when some invocation is eligible. Each eligible RunLarger rewrites only a private copy of that invocation's driver, mounts it read-only over its own staged path, binds observations and existing JSON/Markdown receipt fingerprints to the selected declaration and original and rewritten paths and hashes, preserves arguments, environment, image and original bytes, rejects stale or substituted evidence, propagates cancellation and releases private resources, and retains the existing weakest-result aggregation and timeout/no-claim rules so an actual larger mismatch still fails the gate without erasing independent base evidence. Update docs/python.md with separate-driver configuration examples and per-invocation eligibility and provenance rules, and update SPEC.md with a citation to [#884's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-884.json) under D-0181, D-0185 and D-0199; the README's existing Python-page link and overview remain accurate, and validate the affected Python suites including existing legacy, shared-driver, isolation and receipt coverage with their established real-tool opt-ins, shuffled repeated runs and the race detector.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationPerCheckDrivers884
tests.says: Two targets use distinct drivers, directories, literal arguments and sibling imports at ordinary and larger bounds, with separate authenticated source hashes and read-only overlays, unchanged staged and original bytes, and one image; sampled, legacy and shared-driver configurations still work.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationPerCheckLargerEligibility884
tests.says: Missing bounds or failed base prerequisites suppress only the affected invocation, eligible siblings share one larger TLC run, and a real larger mismatch remains the weakest result and fails the gate.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationPerCheckDriverIsolation884
tests.says: Per-check drivers retain path and selected-source validation, snapshot freshness, authenticated hash checks, complete bound declarations and cancellation cleanup, including outside the manifest driver's directory.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationPerCheckDriverReceipts884
tests.says: Successful, skipped and mismatching per-driver results survive JSON and Markdown receipt round trips, and portable fingerprints bind each invocation, original source, rewritten source and overlay.
